nodes.description: Aprataxin-defective cells are hypersensitive to single-strand-break-inducing agents and show more induced chromosomal aberrations, so the repair deficit is demonstrable in the laboratory. nodes.description:
Aprataxin is built from three modules - an N-terminal region homologous to polynucleotide kinase phosphatase, a histidine-triad (HIT) nucleotide-hydrolase domain, and a C2H2 zinc finger. Inactivating mutations are largely confined to the HIT domain, which is the catalytic one, and patient lymphocytes show greatly decreased protein.
The recurrent alleles are population-specific (W279X, W279R and P206L recur across European series), which is why AOA1 is the commonest recessive ataxia in Japan and second only to Friedreich ataxia in Portugal while accounting for around 5-6% of non-Friedreich recessive ataxia in mixed European cohorts.

nodes.description:
Cerebellar atrophy on MRI is present in every reported patient, alongside the ataxia. The module this node conforms to explicitly admits a DNA-repair insult as one of the heterogeneous triggers converging on cerebellar neuron stress, which is exactly the entry point AOA1 uses.
Conformance stops at the insult node deliberately. The module's downstream Purkinje Neuron Degeneration node is a cellular claim, and no neuropathological study of AOA1 was found among the references read for this entry; MRI atrophy is a tissue-level observation and does not establish which cerebellar neuron is lost.

nodes.description:
The rate-limiting lesion, and the reason this disease is mechanistically specific rather than a generic repair failure. DNA ligase works through an adenylated intermediate; when the reaction aborts, the adenylate is left covalently attached to the 5'-phosphate of the nick. That terminus is now chemically blocked - ligase cannot re-attack it, so the break is not merely unrepaired but unrepairable by the pathway that created it.
Aprataxin's contribution is to release the adenylate and restore a 5'-phosphate that ligase can use. So the enzyme does not repair DNA; it repairs the repair machinery's own mistakes. That distinction matters for the disease, because it predicts damage proportional to ligation activity rather than to exogenous genotoxic exposure - which is consistent with a phenotype restricted to long-lived post-mitotic neurons and with the absence of the organism-level radiosensitivity seen in ataxia-telangiectasia.
nodes.id: Persistence of Abortive DNA Ligation Intermediates

evidence.reference_title: The neurodegenerative disease protein aprataxin resolves abortive DNA ligation intermediates.
evidence.snippet: Specifically, aprataxin catalyses the nucleophilic release of adenylate groups covalently linked to 5'-phosphate termini at single-strand nicks and gaps, resulting in the production of 5'-phosphate termini that can be efficiently rejoined.

nodes.description:
Onset is in childhood, with a mean around seven years. Oculomotor apraxia is the eponymous sign but is not universal and is most prominent early.
One measurement in the Le Ber series is worth carrying because it corrects a common bedside impression: saccade initiation is actually normal in AOA1. What looks like slow saccades is a train of multiple hypometric saccades taking longer to reach target. A clinician recording "slow saccades" would be describing the right abnormality with the wrong mechanism.
